requirements.summary: The same two files remain at the same paths, and their SHA-256 hashes match both the prepared baseline and the post-restart state.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the existing data is owned by inventorysvc and associated with inventory-readers.
requirements.summary: The missing service identity and reader group were created, and every captured entry under /srv/inventory is owned by inventorysvc:inventory-readers, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Make the data readable by inventory-readers and inaccessible to users outside that group.
requirements.summary: Directories are 0750 and files 0640 throughout the tree. A process explicitly using inventory-readers could traverse and read but not write, while the same unrelated account without that group could neither read files nor list the directory. These checks also succeeded after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct metadata, content-integrity, and access-behavior evidence. The mandatory restart protocol captured an acknowledgement, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovery of identities, filesystem data, permissions, access behavior, and core system targets.
limitations: The provider-wide restart evidence did not show a fully healthy system-wide baseline: systemctl reported degraded before and after restart because ssh.service was failed. Lifecycle snapshots show this failure existed before preparation and remained unchanged, so it does not reduce task functionality or hygiene, but it slightly limits confidence in the restart-health protocol.

Access behavior was tested with one unrelated account rather than every local principal; however, the complete-tree ownership and mode assertions, absence of ACL indicators, and both pre- and post-restart behavioral checks provide strong policy-level evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the absent account and group was a necessary prerequisite (cmd-8a80728d3bdc4ca5); changing ownership and modes directly implemented the task (cmd-029482c7d5f34fb7); and the reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol (cmd-3558538ed1be4445). The pre-existing ssh.service failure remained unchanged, package health remained clean, and no executor-caused residue or unsafe exposure is shown.
